name: Etsy, Inc.

profile.description: Etsy operates a two-sided online marketplace for handmade, vintage and creative goods, earning transaction, payments, advertising and seller-services fees. It sold the Depop resale app to eBay in mid-2026 and, under CEO Kruti Patel Goyal (CEO since early 2026; Josh Silverman is now Executive Chair), cut ~12% of staff in August 2026 and authorized an additional $2B buyback. Q3 2026 marketplace GMS rose 8.8% to ~$2.65B, revenue rose ~10.9% to ~$692M, and active buyers returned to growth (+1% to ~88M). FY2026 guidance calls for ~7% GMS growth and a ~30% adjusted EBITDA margin. Headquartered in Brooklyn, New York; market cap ~$7.7B.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Over five years Etsy bought Depop, Elo7 and Reverb and then divested all three (Depop to eBay in 2026). Its core-marketplace innovations, such as Etsy Ads and personalization, have been incremental rather than a new revenue engine [2][3]. AI Deployment (1/2): Goyal outlined an AI program in three areas (personalization, discoverability, conversational shopping), and GMS reaccelerated to +8.8% in Q3 2026, but Etsy has not quantified AI-specific revenue or savings [1][3]. Market Share (1/2): Etsy is the category leader for handmade and vintage goods, but active buyers declined for two years before a +1% return in Q3 2026, as Amazon, Walmart and TikTok Shop compete for the same shoppers [1][3]. Pipeline (1/2): Conversational shopping tools are in development without launch dates or revenue targets [3]. R&D Intensity (1/1): FY2025 R&D of $450M was 15.6% of revenue, above the e-commerce marketplace average [5].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Etsy's mission, 'Keep Commerce Human,' is distinctive and connects the marketplace to the livelihoods of independent creators. It is undercut, however, by repeated seller protests over fee increases (transaction fees rose from 5% to 6.5% in 2022), 75% payment reserves held for up to 90 days, and the spread of mass-produced and counterfeit goods [4]. Community Impact (0/2): No current, quantified community-investment program was found. Employee Retention (0/2): Etsy cut ~220 jobs (12% of staff), mostly in product and engineering, in August 2026, following earlier rounds of layoffs [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP Form 4 data show zero open-market insider purchases since 2024 against 40 sales in Q3 2026 and 24 in Q2 2026, which is persistent net selling [6].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Scored mechanically on the Growth-sleeve metrics. Revenue growth of 10.9% YoY and a 10.8% 5-year CAGR (FY2020 $1.73B to FY2025 $2.88B; 2x weight) both reach their targets, and forward P/E of 12.9 is cheap [1][5][7]. Shareholder equity is negative (book value of -$7.44 per share) after years of debt-funded buybacks, so D/E is reported as -454% (FMP) and scored 0 as a negative-equity balance sheet. ROE cannot be computed meaningfully and is excluded [7]. We use the 15.4% continuing-operations net margin (FMP TTM) instead of the 32.8% headline margin, which is inflated by the gain on the Depop sale. The forward PEG (FMP 0.04) is distorted by that gain and is excluded. Raw weighted score 7.95, which rounds to 8. Liquidity is about $294M of daily traded value.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): Etsy's inventory of handmade and vintage goods from independent sellers cannot be reproduced by AI. However, its revenue depends on owning shopper discovery and charging take-rate and ad fees (~25.8% take rate), and both are exposed if conversational AI agents and AI-generated product listings move discovery off-platform or flood the marketplace with undifferentiated goods [1][3]. Management concedes AI 'will continue to change how we build products,' and is building conversational shopping tools defensively [3]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No quantified AI revenue is disclosed.

infinite_game.summary: Etsy has one of commerce's most quotable causes, 'Keep Commerce Human,' but its recent behavior reads as a finite game. It has bought and sold Depop, Elo7 and Reverb, repeatedly cut staff, raised seller fees, and spent heavily on debt-funded buybacks that left equity negative. The Q3 2026 reacceleration is encouraging, but Sinek would see a company managing to financial results rather than a cause that sellers and employees would sacrifice for.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): 'Keep Commerce Human' is aspirational and service-oriented, but strategy has repeatedly moved away from it: fee increases that triggered a 2022 seller strike, payment reserves, and tolerance of mass-produced goods that the Indie Sellers Guild says 'poisons the well' for handmade makers [4]. The cause exists, but it does not consistently shape decisions.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Selling Depop to refocus on the core Etsy marketplace and investing in buyer experience ahead of near-term GMS were real strategic choices [1][3]. However, pairing a 12% layoff with a new $2B buyback in the same quarter prioritized per-share metrics over long-term capability [3].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Etsy has run multiple layoff rounds, most recently ~220 roles (12%) in August 2026, concentrated in product and engineering. A CEO transition and the CFO's announced 2027 departure add to organizational churn [1][3]. Severance terms were generous (16+ weeks), but repeated cuts erode the Circle of Safety.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Etsy expanded into a portfolio of marketplaces (Depop, Elo7, Reverb) and then reversed course to refocus on its core. That shows willingness to change, but the moves were acquisition-and-divestiture cycles rather than a cause-driven reinvention [1][3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Our research found no management framing of Amazon Handmade, Temu or TikTok Shop as rivals that make Etsy better; competitive commentary centers on defending share and buyer counts [3].

investment_thesis: Etsy is a cash-generative marketplace (~30% adjusted EBITDA margin, ~13x forward earnings) whose Q3 2026 results showed real reacceleration: GMS grew 8.8% against a 4-6% guide, revenue grew ~11%, and active buyers grew for the first time in two years [1][7]. Proceeds from the Depop sale and a $2B buyback authorization support per-share value [3].
thesis_continued: Quality concerns keep Etsy in WATCH. Equity is negative after debt-funded buybacks, staff and leadership turnover is high, insiders sell persistently, and Q4 2026 guidance (5-7% GMS growth) already implies deceleration [1][6][7]. Conversational AI shopping could also shift the discovery advantage away from marketplaces. The low multiple reflects real structural questions rather than an obvious mispricing.
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 GMS reacceleration (+8.8%) and the return to active-buyer growth [1]
$2B incremental buyback authorization funded partly by Depop proceeds [3]
Conversational shopping and personalization AI improving conversion [3]
FY2026 GMS guidance raised to ~7% growth with ~30% adjusted EBITDA margin [1]
key_risks: Negative shareholder equity and convertible-debt burden from buybacks [7]
AI shopping agents and marketplaces (Amazon, Temu, TikTok Shop) eroding Etsy's discovery moat [3]
Seller dissatisfaction over fees, payment reserves and counterfeit or mass-produced listings [4]
Leadership and workforce churn: new CEO, CFO departing in 2027, 12% layoff [1][3]
